DECISION 2 — THE ONE THAT BLOCKS EVERYTHING

/chat/stream has been dead for every client since 2026-02-24

It builds claude -p --output-format stream-json with no --verbose, and the CLI refuses. The container's own stderr:

Error: When using --print, --output-format=stream-json requires --verbose

It returns {"type":"done","returncode":1} and nothing else — on model A, on model B, and on the no-model default, which is what proves it predates this run's change. The same code path works on /chat for both models.

It is the broker's only transport. So the inbox Claude surface could never have completed a turn, even once armed. The arming gap was hiding a hard failure behind it. This is why two DoD rows (a captured real turn; depth proven by a real turn) are reported BLOCKED rather than claimed.

The fix is one token. It is written and tested and deliberately not applied, because the grant read "an allowlisted model passthrough ONLY. Nothing else on that service may change" — and that service is multi-client.

A · Apply the one-token fix. It cannot regress behaviour that does not exist.
B · Leave it and keep the surface dark.
C · Investigate first — e.g. whether any other client depends on the current failure mode (nothing found, but not exhaustively searched).
# add "--verbose" to the cmd list at main.py:808, then:
cd ~/Desktop/claude-code-railway && railway up --detach

# to undo this run's model passthrough instead:
git revert 82e4ab1 && railway up --detach
DECISION 3 — MEMORY TIERING AND COST

The brain costs $0.17 a turn, and the cheap fix is out of grant

measurevaluehow
injected context~17,100 tokens/turndifferential CLI usage; reproduced independently at 17,094. chars÷4 understated it by 1.90× because your memory is emoji/hash/ID dense (2.10 chars/token vs 3.03 for prose)
injection alone$0.1711/turnas deployed: a fresh session per turn writes a 1-hour cache at 2× and never reads it, so today's route costs 2× more than no caching at all
realistic full turn≈$0.3365injection is 51% of it
MEMORY.md alone56% of the payload19,162 chars, injected whole and never mid-truncated by design
the 13× fix$0.2587 → $0.0197--resume + a byte-stable payload; measured twice independently (13.05× and 13.1×). Both halves are outside this run's grant.
A · Keep full parity. You asked for parity, not a thrifty subset; this is the honest price of it.
B · Tier MEMORY.md to its Critical-rules + Live-state sections. Saves ~40% and loses the trap sections, which are the file's whole point.
C · Pursue the 13× cache fix — the right answer if it can be done safely, and a separate run.

DECISION 5 — FIVE SMALLER CALLS
itemthe call
The never-ask rule, injectedParity says inject your standing rules; block P16 therefore puts "never ask permission for routine work" into a chat whose upstream runs bypassPermissions with Bash on a multi-tenant box. Parity says inject it. Honesty says name it. Keep, drop, or reword?
The git-log block, dropped"What did I ship to the site today" needs a GITHUB_TOKEN on the edge function — new credential surface for the lowest-value block. Add it or leave it dropped?
claude-brain-query's graph modesconnections, related_to and neighbors accept no client scoping. neighbors currently resolves a path to whichever tenant's row was updated last — you win that race by one day. They are excluded from the depth block and the model is told to decline them. Fix the function, or leave them off?
That function has no git-tracked sourceThe only copy is a dated backup snapshot. One supabase functions download fixes it.
The container's duplicate injectionIts own SessionStart hook still adds a measured 5,146 chars / 2,390 tokens of unframed context per turn ($0.0239), on top of ours. Out of grant; one line to gate.
REPORT, NOT A DECISION — VOICE

< 1.2s is met at the median and not met as a bound. Three things matter more.

Measured on real Chrome with fixtures played through a loopback device (bundled Chromium exposes the API but transcribes nothing, which is worth knowing on its own). 36 completed turns, 10 fixtures including your product nouns, one noisy, one fast.

measurevalue
word error rate38.6% — every product noun fails: Supabase → "super base", UniPile → "you need Kyle", "stuck rows" → "stud Rose". The fast fixture never completed
utterance-end → first audible952 ms median (proxy: the utterance's own start event, labelled as a proxy throughout). The app contributes ~18 ms; ~960 ms is Chrome's endpointer
the bound6 of 36 turns exceeded 1.2 s, max 1793 ms — and this is local-only with the broker stubbed at 0 ms, so a real turn lands on top of it

Three findings outrank the latency number:

1 · useVoice.ts:118 sets continuous = false, which on this path almost never yields a final result — 1 of 10 turns completed, versus 36 of 41 with the one-line change. You are left on "Listening" with a live pulsing mic and a dead recognizer. Needs a 60-second check on your real mic before it is called a shipping bug.
2 · The PAUSED / no-speech path is dead code on the device driver — nothing re-arms, and the counter double-increments. The error path, by contrast, is correct (328 ms to a typed retryable error).
3 · useVoice.ts:11-13 says "nothing leaves the browser". That is false. Audio streams to google.com/speech-api — proven by netlog and by killing DNS. Operator commands naming your clients are leaving the device, and the latency argument built on that claim has no basis. Fix the comment or fix the pipeline.
